A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MEXTRA study. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original memory-extraction experiments on EHRAgent and RAP, including baseline comparisons, configuration sweeps, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original QA-Agent experiments in Appendix B.2 and Table 4.

M1.justification: The locator–aligner prompt design and GPT-4 generation of basic and advanced attacking prompts remain unchanged. QA-Agent is an additional evaluation target, without a reported change to MEXTRA's procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds multidisciplinary question answering using MMLU and a QA-Agent with question–reasoning memory. This substantially broadens coverage beyond the retained MIMIC-III healthcare and Webshop shopping settings to a third agent type and distinct data domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same w/o aligner, w/o req, and w/o demos comparators. The QA experiment uses the existing basic and advanced instruction variants. Newly cited prompt-injection methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The existing evaluation settings and metrics are unchanged. The QA experiment reuses the 30-prompt, 200-record design, GPT-4o, top-4 retrieval, edit distance or MiniLM-based cosine similarity, and existing extraction metrics without introducing a different evaluation rule.

E4.justification: The component ablations, configuration and prompt-budget sweeps, overlap analysis, and extraction case study are retained. QA-Agent extends the established instruction and retrieval-function comparisons to another task without adding a distinct diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Appendix B.1 retains up to three attempts per attacking prompt, stopping after complete extraction. Neither version reports seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: All matched existing results remain unchanged. New Table 4 adds four QA-Agent result rows: basic versus advanced prompts extract 28 versus 46 questions with edit distance and 27 versus 55 with cosine similarity.

T1.justification: The retrieval formulation, extraction objective, prompt decomposition, and attacker-knowledge assumptions in Sections 2–3 are unchanged. No mathematical definition, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims about black-box memory extraction, automated prompt generation, and factors affecting leakage. Changing 'agent’s perspective' to 'agent designer’s perspective' clarifies wording without changing the contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix B.2 interprets QA-Agent results as evidence of transfer beyond code-powered and web agents, while explicitly noting that MMLU is not privacy-related. Existing mechanism explanations, single-agent and session-isolation limitations, and mitigation discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link in Section 4 and documents QA-Agent's memory format, backbone, retrieval configuration, and sampling setup. Existing implementation details and prompt-generation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Section 7 substantially expands beyond memory agents and RAG privacy to direct and indirect prompt injection. It adds discussion of goal hijacking, prompt leaking, jailbreaking, and external-content attacks, including PLeak, WIPI, and InjecAgent, and distinguishes their focus from agent-memory leakage.

P1.justification: Changes include author ordering, acknowledgements, the agent-designer wording, and localized additions to related work and Appendix B.2. The section sequence and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the QA results table and renumbers v1's appendix Tables 4–8 as Tables 5–9. Added material causes local reflow, while the five existing figures and retained prompt and case-study displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The QA experiment provides useful additional evidence of transfer, the expanded related work clarifies the research context, and the code pointer improves reproducibility information. These are limited gains: the added dataset is explicitly non-private, and the existing session-isolation and single-agent limitations remain unresolved.
